# pushpage

pushpage is a service that accepts HTML and returns a shareable public URL. It is purpose-built for AI agents: instead of dumping HTML or long-form content into chat, an agent publishes to pushpage and hands the user a clean, clickable link.

## Quick rules for agents

1. **If the pushpage MCP tools are available** (`publish_page`, `update_page`, `list_pages`, `delete_page`, `health`; in Claude Code they appear as `mcp__pushpage__publish_page` and so on), **use them and do NOT ask the user for an API key.** Authentication is handled by the MCP client.
2. **If a tool answers that sign-in is needed** (Claude Code: `MCP server "pushpage" needs you to sign in again (run /mcp to re-authenticate)`, or a `401` / Connect prompt in another client), tell the user to run `/mcp` in Claude Code, pick pushpage and choose Authenticate (other clients: complete the browser sign-in they show), then retry once. Do not retry in a loop.
3. **If the MCP tools are not available**, offer to connect them (see "Connect the MCP server" below). Use the REST API with an API key only as a fallback (see "REST API fallback").
4. Return the page `url` to the user. Never paste the HTML into chat.

## Constraints

- **Pages are public.** Anyone with the URL can read the page. Never publish content that contains secrets, credentials, personal data, or anything the user has not explicitly chosen to share.
- **Max payload:** 1 MB per request (app-level limit; the servlet ceiling is 10 MB but the app rejects above 1 MB).
- **Rate limits:** signed-in users — 10 publishes/min; guests (no account) — 5 publishes/min per IP. Admin users are exempt.
- **Page retention:** guest pages auto-expire after 30 minutes. Pages of signed-in users persist for 30 days (default; depends on the plan) and are managed from the dashboard.
- **Format:** HTML only. Pages are served directly in a browser — write clean, self-contained HTML (inline CSS, no local file references).

## Base URL

Base URL resolution (pick the first that applies):
1. If `APP_SERVER_URL` is configured in the environment → use it.
2. Otherwise, use `https://pushpage.link` (the managed public instance).

Concrete fallback used in all examples below: `https://pushpage.link`

**HTTPS required:** the public instance (`pushpage.link`) requires HTTPS. Never downgrade to `http://pushpage.link` — requests will fail. Self-hosted instances may use HTTP if that is how `APP_SERVER_URL` is configured.

## Connect the MCP server (recommended)

The MCP server is at `https://pushpage.link/mcp` (streamable-http transport; self-hosted: `{APP_SERVER_URL}/mcp`). It exposes `publish_page`, `update_page`, `list_pages`, `delete_page` and `health`. Preference order:

1. **MCP with browser sign-in (recommended).** Connect to `/mcp` with the URL alone; no key to copy. Publishing works immediately as a guest and never prompts, so pages that are only published silently expire after 30 minutes: to sign in, ask the agent to list the user's pages (any account-only call) before publishing pages the user wants to keep. The first time a tool that needs an account is called (`list_pages`, `update_page`, `delete_page`), the server answers `401` and a client that supports MCP sign-in prompts the user to sign in in the browser. One approval grants publish, update, list and delete, and the user can revoke it under Account → Connected apps in the dashboard.
2. **MCP as a guest (no account, "try it").** `/mcp-guest` never prompts. `publish_page` works and the page expires after 30 minutes; the tool result has `guest_mode: true`, a `message` and `signup_url` — relay the message so the user knows how to sign in (on `/mcp-guest` it explains to re-add the server with `/mcp`).
3. **MCP with an API key** — for headless/CI setups, the local `uvx pushpage-mcp` stdio server (no browser flow there) and clients that cannot do browser sign-in.
4. **REST API** — for scripts and non-MCP integrations (see the fallback below).

### Claude Code (browser sign-in)

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http pushpage https://pushpage.link/mcp
```

The first call to `list_pages`, `update_page` or `delete_page` fails once with `MCP server "pushpage" needs you to sign in again (run /mcp to re-authenticate)`. The user runs `/mcp`, picks pushpage and chooses Authenticate; after one approval list, update, delete and publish all work. If `update_page` still reports a missing permission, the app was connected before updates existed: remove it under Account → Connected apps and connect again.

Only Claude Code and the MCP Inspector are confirmed to work with the sign-in flow. Other clients that support MCP sign-in may work; if a client cannot sign in, use `/mcp-guest` (publish only) or an API key.

### Try it with no account (guest mode)

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http pushpage https://pushpage.link/mcp-guest
```

### Headless / CI / clients without browser sign-in (API key)

Create a named key under Account → API keys in `https://pushpage.link/dashboard` (one key per agent) and send it as the `X-Api-Key` header (or `Authorization: Bearer pp_...`).

Claude Desktop config (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` on macOS, `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` on Windows):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pushpage": {
      "type": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://pushpage.link/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "X-Api-Key": "<your-api-key>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude Desktop after saving. Claude Desktop does not expand environment variables in `headers`; Claude Code (`${PUSHPAGE_API_KEY}`) and Cursor (`${env:PUSHPAGE_API_KEY}`) do, so prefer that to pasting the key. Never commit the key to git. Store a key file with owner-only permissions: `mkdir -p ~/.config/pushpage && umask 077 && printf '%s' 'pp_...' > ~/.config/pushpage/credentials && chmod 600 ~/.config/pushpage/credentials`.

Local stdio server (no browser sign-in; needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pushpage": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["pushpage-mcp"],
      "env": { "PUSHPAGE_API_KEY": "<your-api-key>" }
    }
  }
}
```

Any client that supports streamable-http MCP servers can connect to `https://pushpage.link/mcp`; consult its documentation for the config format. `https://pushpage.link/mcp/signin` is deprecated: do not recommend it.

## Using the MCP tools

- `publish_page(html, title?)` → `{ url, id, expires_at }`. `title` is optional (taken from the HTML `<title>`, falling back to "Untitled").
- `update_page(id, html, title?)` → same `url` and `id`; use it to change a page you already published instead of creating a duplicate. Needs an account; guest pages cannot be updated.
- `list_pages()` → your pages (`id`, `title`, `url`, `created_at`, `expires_at`). Needs an account.
- `delete_page(id)` → deletes one of your pages. Needs an account.
- `health()` → service status.

Return the `url` to the user. That is the shareable link.

## REST API fallback

Use this only when the MCP tools are not available and the user cannot or does not want to connect them. It is for scripts and non-MCP integrations. It needs an API key for anything except guest publishing.

### Credentials (REST only)

```bash
PUSHPAGE_API_KEY=$(cat ~/.config/pushpage/credentials 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
```

If the file is missing or empty, tell the user (preferably offer the MCP connection above instead of a key):

> Your pushpage API key is not configured. Run the following to save it:
> ```bash
> mkdir -p ~/.config/pushpage && echo "pp_your_key_here" > ~/.config/pushpage/credentials
> ```
> You can create a key in the pushpage dashboard under Account → API keys (give each agent its own named key), or find the "Bootstrap key" in the startup logs of a self-hosted instance.

Pass the key in every authenticated request as `X-Api-Key: $PUSHPAGE_API_KEY`.

**Guest publishing:** `POST /api/pages` accepts requests with no API key. The page is a guest page that auto-expires after 30 minutes. Use it for quick one-off shares when no credentials are available.

**New users:** `POST https://pushpage.link/api/auth/signup` with `{"email": "...", "password": "..."}` returns `201 No Content`; the user then signs in at `https://pushpage.link/dashboard` to connect an agent or create an API key.

### Publish HTML

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://pushpage.link/api/pages \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $PUSHPAGE_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"html": "<html>...</html>"}'
```

`title` is optional. When omitted or blank, the server extracts it from the HTML `<title>` tag; falls back to `"Untitled"`.

Response:

```json
{
  "url": "https://pushpage.link/pages/abc123.html",
  "id": "abc123",
  "expires_at": "2026-07-11T10:00:00Z"
}
```

File upload variant: `curl -s -X POST https://pushpage.link/api/pages -H "X-Api-Key: $PUSHPAGE_API_KEY" -F "file=@report.html"`

### Other operations

```bash
# List (regular users see their own pages; admins see all)
curl -s https://pushpage.link/api/pages -H "X-Api-Key: $PUSHPAGE_API_KEY"

# Delete
curl -s -X DELETE https://pushpage.link/api/pages/{id} -H "X-Api-Key: $PUSHPAGE_API_KEY"

# Update in place (same id and URL; expiry restarts; counts toward the publish rate limit)
curl -s -X PUT https://pushpage.link/api/pages/{id} \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Api-Key: $PUSHPAGE_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"html": "<!DOCTYPE html>...new content...", "title": "Optional new title"}'

# Health check (no auth)
curl -s https://pushpage.link/api/health
```

Update replaces the HTML of one of your pages (admins: any user page). Guest pages cannot be updated (403): publish a new page instead. Full reference: `https://pushpage.link/docs` and the Swagger UI at `https://pushpage.link/api/swagger-ui/index.html`.

## Writing good HTML for pushpage

Pages are served directly in a browser — write clean, self-contained HTML:

- Use inline CSS — no external stylesheets
- Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` for mobile responsiveness
- Include a `<title>` tag — it appears in the browser tab and is used as the page title in the dashboard
- No references to local files; everything must be self-contained
- Tailwind via CDN works well: `<script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com"></script>`
- Charts: Chart.js CDN works well for data visualisations

## Typical agent flow

1. Build the full HTML for what the user asked for — include a `<title>` tag in the `<head>`.
2. Call `publish_page(html=...)` (MCP). If the tools are missing, offer the MCP connection; fall back to `POST /api/pages` only if needed.
3. Return the `url` from the result to the user — do not paste the HTML into chat. If the result has `guest_mode: true`, also relay its `message` (30-minute page; how to sign in for permanent pages).
4. To change that page later, call `update_page(id, html=...)`. If it needs sign-in, follow rule 2 at the top.

## Do not

- Do not ask the user for an API key when the MCP tools are available.
- Do not publish pages that contain secrets, credentials, or private data — pages are publicly accessible to anyone with the link.
- Do not create duplicate pages for the same content — use `update_page` (REST: `PUT /api/pages/{id}`) to change a page you already published; its URL stays the same.
- Do not use `http://` with the managed instance — HTTPS only.
- Do not exceed 1 MB of HTML in a single request — split into multiple pages if needed.
